text:
sara_support: FYI received an urgent report from a customer who upgraded their app and is hitting 404s + param errors from the TS/Node SDK after an SDK upgrade. Node 18, @redwood/sdk install shows 0.21 in package.json but they see 0.19 in lockfile.

ben_eng: Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact error body?

sara_support: Pasting minimal repro they shared:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'gpt-redwood-1', session: 's-123', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }] });
```
Response: 404, body: { "error": "route not found", "code": 404 }

arya_client_sdk: That pattern rings a bell — API route names changed in the new surface. chat.create -> messages.generate and param `session` was renamed to `chat_session`. If the published runtime doesn't map the old method/param names, callers will 404 or get 400 for unknown params.

ben_eng: Two quick checks: 1) npm ls @redwood/sdk (or check node_modules/@redwood/sdk/package.json) to confirm what version actually got installed at runtime. 2) Try a direct HTTP call to the v1 endpoint as a repro: `POST /v1/messages.generate` with the new param name to verify the backend behavior.

sara_support: Customer ran `npm ls @redwood/sdk` and it printed 0.19 (lockfile pin). They say `package.json` shows 0.21 but CI used the lockfile. After forcing a fresh install (rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm i) they now hit a 400 with body: { "error": "invalid parameter: session" } (so the SDK is calling messages.generate but sending legacy param).

arya_client_sdk: Ok that clarifies: two separate issues — (A) lockfile mismatch causing old runtime to be used, (B) SDK runtime in 0.21 didn't include the runtime shim for `session`->`chat_session`. I pushed a compatibility hotfix in the client that maps legacy keys to new ones and falls back to calling the legacy route if present. Workarounds for the customer: upgrade to 0.21.1 (contains shim) OR set header `x-rw-sdk-compat: legacy-session` to enable mapping server-side for now.

ben_eng: @arya_client_sdk can you open a tiny PR to add an integration test that simulates a lockfile installing an older version and ensure our guidance is in the changelog? Also add a note to the migration doc about `chat.create` -> `messages.generate` and `session` -> `chat_session`.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: npm release 0.21.1 -> canary (build 2026-03-17_09:12)

sara_support: Great, I'll send the customer three paths: 1) quick workaround: set header `x-rw-sdk-compat: legacy-session` on requests; 2) reinstall with lockfile reset to pick up 0.21.1; 3) if blocked, use direct HTTP POST to /v1/messages.generate as a temp patch.

arya_client_sdk: I'll attach repro steps to the ticket (include package-lock.json and npm ls output). Also adding a short snippet for the workaround:
```http
POST /v1/messages.generate
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer <key>, 'x-rw-sdk-compat': 'legacy-session' }
Body: { model: 'gpt-redwood-1', chat_session: 's-123', messages: [...] }
```

sara_support: Thanks — marking customer as escalated and adding ETA to ticket. :thumbsup:
